hi-oha-oahu-2026-akaka-kalei.name: Kalei Akaka
hi-oha-oahu-2026-akaka-kalei.bio: Office of Hawaiian Affairs Oʻahu Trustee since 2018; previously worked at the Hawaiʻi State Legislature in both the House and Senate.

hi-oha-oahu-2026-wong-hinaleimoana.name: Hinaleimoana (Hina) Wong
hi-oha-oahu-2026-wong-hinaleimoana.bio: Native Hawaiian cultural practitioner, educator, filmmaker, haku mele (composer) and community advocate.

positions.stance: Says that as Native Hawaiians face challenges in housing, education, cultural preservation and economic opportunity, "OHA must continue to be a strong, trusted, and effective advocate for our people."
Committed to "listening, bringing people together, and ensuring that Native Hawaiian values guide the decisions that shape our future."
Looks forward to "protecting our ʻāina and kaiāulu, ensuring that Hawaiʻi will remain our mainland for our future generations."

hi-oha-maui-2026-lindsey-carmen.name: Carmen Hulu Lindsey
hi-oha-maui-2026-lindsey-carmen.bio: Office of Hawaiian Affairs Maui Trustee since 2012 (Board chair 2021–2024) and a licensed real estate agent for more than 30 years.

positions.stance: Fights to ensure Native Hawaiians receive "their rightful share of ceded land trust revenues and that our homelands are never surrendered."
"Every Hawaiian family deserves a place to call home"; prioritizes the Hawaiian Home Lands waitlist, affordable housing and anti-displacement protections.
Committed to ensuring Maui's recovery "is led by and for the community," including mental health and kūpuna support.
Believes protecting the environment is inseparable from protecting Native Hawaiian rights and that "OHA must be a leading voice for environmental justice."
Advocates for Hawaiian language education and cultural preservation so every Native Hawaiian keiki has "an education that honors who they are."

mt-sc4-2026-eddy-amy.name: Amy Eddy
mt-sc4-2026-eddy-amy.bio: Montana District Court Judge since 2015, elected three times by Flathead County voters.

positions.stance: "I believe deeply that we must keep politics out of the courtroom."
Says the Supreme Court "is not a legislature and not a campaign battleground—it is a court of law" where outcomes are determined by the facts and the law.
Believes the rule of law "is the foundation of a free society, and it must be protected," and that a consistent rule of law provides stability.

mt-sc4-2026-wilson-dan.name: Dan Wilson
mt-sc4-2026-wilson-dan.bio: Flathead County District Court judge since 2016; former Justice of the Peace, prosecutor and private-practice attorney.

positions.stance: "Montana's courts should serve the people — not political agendas."
Describes himself as a constitutional conservative who will "protect the rights of every Montanan as guaranteed by the Constitution."
Will apply Montana's laws "faithfully as written," with no rulings that substitute a judge's preferences for the will of the people.

nd-sc-2026-tufte-jerod.name: Jerod Tufte
nd-sc-2026-tufte-jerod.bio: Justice of the North Dakota Supreme Court since 2017; former district court judge, Kidder County State's Attorney, legal counsel to the Governor and National Guard Judge Advocate.

positions.stance: Brings "an analytical, text-first approach"; "applies the law as written and decides the case in front of him without making promises about the next one."
"A Supreme Court that decides cases carefully, consistently, and without political pressure protects the rule of law for every North Dakotan."

nd-sc-2026-johnson-ariston.name: Ariston E Johnson
nd-sc-2026-johnson-ariston.bio: Attorney in private practice since 2007, McKenzie County Assistant State's Attorney and general counsel to McKenzie Electric Cooperative.

positions.stance: Says judicial elections "are not about politics or policy" but about trust that judges will apply the law faithfully and respect the other branches.
Whenever parties, lawyers, or judges have something to say about a case, "I will listen and ensure that I understand their position before making my mind up."
"My judicial philosophy is built on humility and restraint"; judges should not assume they know what the law should be better than the political branches.
"The judiciary does not exist to second-guess any of that work, but rather to preserve the rule of law throughout the process."
